title: Common English subject codes are exported as lowercase aliases

evidence.quote: // Excludes common words that are also subject codes (IS, UP, ME, etc.)

reasoning: The file documents that common English words which are also subject codes should be unsafe for lowercase matching, but several common words are still exported as lowercase subject aliases and are absent from the unsafe set. Consumers that exact-match SUBJECT_ALIASES will treat ordinary prose like "last semester", "career path", "lead discussion", "port", or "scan" as subject filters for LAST, PATH, LEAD, PORT, or SCAN, which can incorrectly narrow search results.
reproduction: Match or extract a query containing one of these standalone lowercase words, such as "last semester" or "career path"; the alias data exposes "last" and "path" as subject aliases even though they are common English words.
recommendation: Add these common-word subject codes to the unsafe lowercase list in the generator/source data, regenerate valid-subjects.ts so their lowercase code aliases are omitted, and keep only unambiguous full department-name aliases where appropriate.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no linked tests. Adjacent subject/alias tests cover some unsafe lowercase examples such as IS, ME, UP, art, and law, but they do not cover LAST, LEAD, PATH, PORT, SCAN, or common prose containing those words.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add extractor or alias-registry cases asserting that "last semester", "career path", "lead discussion", "scan open classes", and "port" do not produce subject hints, while uppercase explicit subject-code queries like "LAST courses" still do.
minimumFixScope: Update the unsafe lowercase subject-code blocklist and regenerate apps/api/src/services/data/valid-subjects.ts; add focused alias/extractor regression tests for the newly unsafe codes.
